findings: Merge of five source changes that were each accepted on their own. The q01, q02, q09 and q19 parts went in unchanged. I reviewed the hand-applied q18 hunks and the places where they meet the other changes.

physical_hash_join.cpp CastJoinFilterValueToStorage: computes value + offset in HUGEINT with TryAdd, then casts to the storage type. If either step fails, the IN/range filter is skipped and the min/max filter is skipped too (`continue`). So an out-of-range key cannot produce a wrong filter. NULLs are passed through unchanged and are then rejected by the existing ContainsNull/IsNull checks.

Range-set split in PushInFilter: it relies on the in_list being sorted. FilterCombiner::IsDenseRange does sort it for integral, non-UHUGEINT types, and the new code also excludes HUGEINT and UHUGEINT, so the hugeint gap subtraction cannot overflow. Taking more keys than the threshold means gaps.size() >= max_filter_count > split_count, so the nth_element bound is valid. The ranges cover every key and are wrapped in OptionalFilter, so the filter is a superset and only prunes. Correctness does not depend on it.

join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp: pushing through __internal_compress_integral_* only happens with a constant, non-null offset, integer types of 64 bits or less, and at most one offset per column. The UNION rewrite carries storage_offset forward. Every other pass-through case reuses the same column struct, so the offset is never lost before the probe value is mapped back to the storage value. The bloom filter is turned off when an offset is set (has_cast), because it hashes join-key values, not storage values.

CanUseInFilter now allows up to 64x the dynamic OR threshold (about 3200 keys at the default). The extra cost is a bounded scan of the hash-table keys at build finalize. Non-integral types above the threshold return early.
SEMI-join cardinality and HAVING range-selectivity changes only affect estimates and join order. They depend on general plan properties, not on names or literals.
data_table.cpp MaxThreads: smaller morsels let the scan use up to the configured thread count. It does not exceed the user's thread setting.
None of the conditions reference tables, columns, literals or dataset sizes. No measurement, settings defaults or tests are touched.
